name: Eben am Achensee
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny high plateau at the Achensee, with a family-friendly ski area and a stunning turquoise-blue lake right on your doorstep.
beschreibung:
Overview

Eben am Achensee is situated on a sunny plateau at an altitude of 970 meters in the district of Schwaz, bordering the southern shore of Lake Achensee. Home to around 3,500 residents, the municipality comprises the renowned districts of Maurach, Pertisau, and Eben. Wedged dramatically between the rugged peaks of the Karwendel mountains to the west and the craggy Rofan range to the east, Eben serves as the vibrant hub around Tyrol's largest alpine lake. Whether enjoying sailing, kitesurfing, and lake bathing in summer or gliding along cross-country ski trails and downhill pistes in winter, Eben delivers outstanding alpine recreation throughout the year.

History

Settlement in the valley dates back to the early Middle Ages, with Eben first documented in 1112 in a donation charter granted by the nobles of Schlitters to St. Georgenberg monastery. For centuries, the rich fisheries and forests served as royal hunting grounds for Tyrolean sovereigns, including Emperor Maximilian I. The town's historical identity is inextricably tied to Saint Notburga of Rattenberg (c. 1265–1313), the revered patron saint of peasants, servant maids, and Sunday rest. According to legend, an oxcart carried her remains to Eben, where she was entombed. The current pilgrimage church of Saint Notburga was constructed between 1736 and 1738 by master architect Jakob Singer, featuring an ornate glass shrine containing the saint's relics. The adjacent Notburga Museum illuminates her life and legacy. In the late nineteenth century, tourism boomed with the inauguration of passenger steamboats in 1887 and the opening of the Achensee Cog Railway in 1889, Europe's oldest continuously steam-operated cog railway.

Getting There

By car, Eben is accessed via the Inntal motorway A12 at the Wiesing/Achensee exit, followed by a ten-minute drive up the panoramic B181 highway over the Kanzelkehre curves to Eben and Maurach. Visitors from Bavaria can arrive toll-free via Tegernsee and the Achen Pass or via Bad Tölz and the Sylvenstein reservoir. By rail, travelers alight at the Jenbach transport hub, connected directly to major ICE, Railjet, and Eurocity lines. From Jenbach station, VVT regional bus line 8332 operates every half hour to Eben, Maurach, and Pertisau. In summer, the historic Achensee steam railway provides scenic transfers from Jenbach up to the Seespitz boat landing. Regional buses are free for visitors holding the local AchenseeCard guest card.

Tips

Ride the Rofanseilbahn cable car from Maurach up to 1,840 meters, where the thrilling AirRofan skyglider and diverse climbing routes await adventurous mountaineers. In Pertisau, the Karwendel cable car ascends Zwölferkopf, revealing spectacular panoramic lake vistas. Easy hiking and cycling trails lead into pristine Karwendel side valleys towards the Gramaialm and Gernalm pastures. Cultural highlights include the Saint Notburga Pilgrimage Church and the Vitalberg Shale Oil Museum in Pertisau, showcasing the regional heritage of black oil distillation. For relaxation, the modern lakeside Atoll Achensee center in Maurach offers infinity pools, saunas, and watersports access.
